Team,

Following the close of Q4 reviews yesterday, the people ops team surfaced 14 appeals and ~7 manager-flagged rating discrepancies across Eng and Product. I attached the initial appeal_log_20261130.xlsx with a short note per row (column: summary + urgency).

High level asks:
- Can each manager below review rows assigned to them and add brief context in the "manager_notes" column by EOD Thu 12/3?
- If you believe a change to a rating is warranted, put the proposed delta and a short rationale. HR will consolidate and triage.

Important process notes from Neha (copied):
- Appeals window is open for 10 business days; after that HR closes for this cycle.
- We will only accept appeals tied to process errors (eligibility, calibration mishandling, clear evidence of missed contributions).

Attachments referenced: appeal_log_20261130.xlsx (master), manager_comments_2026.pdf (examples of acceptable evidence), appeals_rubric_v2.docx (working draft).

Please flag any blockers — I want to avoid ad-hoc rating swaps without documented rationale.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad

Thanks Mina. A few proposals from my side that might reduce churn: 

- Tier appeals into three buckets: (A) Process error (eligibility, missed evidence) — auto-accept for review; (B) Substantive disagreement about impact (requires manager rebuttal + 2 peer notes); (C) Administrative request (typo, level classification) — quick fix.
- For (B) we should require a short "appeal packet" (1 page) attached to the appeal row with specific examples and dates; this will reduce back-and-forth.
- Suggest we create a rolling 5-person panel (2 managers from adjacent teams + 1 cross-functional lead + Neha + one HR consultant) to adjudicate (B) within 5 business days.

I can draft the panel rotation and update the rubric doc to reflect the buckets.

—Maya
VP, Engineering Productivity

Adding HR guidance and updated rubric (attached: appeals_rubric_v2.docx). Quick answers to Karthik's questions: 

1) If peer and manager notes conflict, managers should attempt to reconcile with peers within 48 hours. If reconciliation fails, escalate the row to the panel as Maya suggests — HR will mark it as "panel_required".

2) Proposed rating deltas should be manager-endorsed. ICs will be notified and given a chance to provide additional evidence to HR (not to challenge the manager directly). HR has final sign-off for process compliance; changes are applied only after panel sign-off when required.

Operational timeline (summary):
- Appeals window: 11/30 — 12/14 (10 business days)
- Manager context due: by 12/03 EOD
- Panel reviews: 12/06 — 12/10 (for rows marked panel_required)
- Finalization and communication: by 12/15

I've also uploaded an editable appeal form to DocuSign and a consolidated tracker (link below). Please do NOT make rating changes in Workday directly until HR confirms.

Neha Kapoor
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference
